text: Lesson 29 left us with a checklist. This lesson turns the Incident, Problem, and Change rows into real configuration at Caldwell Precision Manufacturing, each decision traced back to one specific stakeholder sentence.

The VP of Operations said Meridian down means back up in under an hour. That becomes three decisions. A Priority Lookup Rule where company-wide impact on Meridian or its dependencies calculates to Priority 1 automatically, with no agent guessing severity under pressure. An Assignment Rule that routes a Meridian Priority 1 straight to the ERP Basis group instead of the general queue, because general triage eats into that one-hour target. And a Major Incident trigger scoped specifically to Priority 1 against Meridian, firing a bridge call and a status cadence to the VP's own distribution list, because under an hour is a communication commitment too.

The plant IT manager's complaint was the Line 3 label printer reopening over and over. The fix is recognizing six separate Incidents describe one condition and linking all of them to a single Problem record through problem_id. Cause notes track what's actually been tested as the investigation runs its real course. Once the network team finds a failing switch port, fix notes document the permanent fix, root cause points at that specific CI, and the Problem becomes a Known Error other agents can search before opening a new investigation at all.

The CFO wanted nobody touching Meridian's production configuration without approval and a record of what changed. A risk questionnaire asks real conditions — production environment, a tested backout plan, whether this exact change has run successfully before. Those answers calculate risk, and Medium or High risk on a Meridian change auto-chains into full CAB review. A routine, already-templated monthly patch still runs as Standard, because that category was authorized once, up front.

Incident, Problem, and Change are now configured against Caldwell's own real requirements. Next, Lesson 31 builds the SLA definitions, the self-service catalog, the knowledge base, and the portal widget that prove those commitments are actually being met.
